transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Out on the trails and even back in town, I keep hearing and sensing things from the landscape telling me what to do with my work, and it’s starting to scare me. It feels so incredibly real, and I just don't know what to do.
Have you been experiencing significant periods of feeling extremely high, unusually irritable, or deeply depressed, and did those mood changes occur at the same time as these voices?

Yes, I've had these wild swings where I feel incredibly high and energetic, followed by crashing into a heavy, gray depression. Interestingly, the voices and the feeling of a special mission only happened during that revved-up high phase; they completely stopped once I hit this low point, even though the depression is still here.
During the times when you were not experiencing the high or low mood swings, did you still have any of these voices or unusual beliefs?

No, not at all. Those voices and beliefs only showed up during that intense, revved-up phase when I was barely sleeping and running on high energy. Once I crashed into the depression, they completely stopped, and I've never had them when my mood was normal.
During those times when you were deeply depressed, did you ever experience any thoughts of wanting to end your life or feelings of worthlessness?

I haven't had any thoughts of wanting to end my life, but the feelings of worthlessness and guilt have been incredibly heavy. I constantly feel like a selfish fraud who ruined the studio and everyone's chances, and like I just deserve to lose everything.

During those high-energy periods, did your beliefs about having a special mission ever lead you to engage in risky behaviors, such as spending excessive money or making impulsive, life-altering decisions?

Yes, absolutely. I was so convinced of my genius and this mission that I signed a studio lease, took on overwhelming loans, and booked festivals without even checking the dates. I didn't even bother making a business plan because I thought my talent alone would make me famous, which has now left my studio's finances in complete disarray.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits clear manic episodes characterized by grandiosity, reduced need for sleep, and impulsive behavior leading to functional impairment, accompanied by psychotic features (hallucinations/delusions). Crucially, the psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during the manic phase, which supports a diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder rather than Schizoaffective Disorder.
